title: PR stochastic load guardrail: Bayesian change detector for perf regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight CI gate that detects performance regressions using stochastic sampling of PR workloads and a Bayesian sequential change-detection model. Unlike the current deterministic baseline snapshot approach, this ticket designs and ships an autosampler that draws small, randomized minibatches of representative traces (varying sequence lengths and prompt classes) from the nightly corpus, runs them through the bench-runner in a controlled environment, and feeds per-run metrics into a Bayesian model that outputs a probabilistic regression score. The goal is a low-noise, fast-running PR check (~5–10 minute extra wall time) that raises a high-confidence regression flag when p95 tokens/sec drops or p95 latency increases beyond the modeled posterior threshold. The system must integrate with GitHub PR checks and the existing metrics-store/bench-history, produce human-readable explanations, and provide a lightweight visualization link in the PR check to the recent posterior and raw sample summaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) GitHub PR check runs on each PR and completes within 10 minutes extra for typical PRs. 2) Detector reports a probabilistic regression score and a pass/fail decision based on configurable posterior threshold. 3) For injected synthetic regressions (bench harness mutation), the detector triggers fail in >= 95% of trials. 4) Raw sample results are persisted to metrics-store and visible in the perf-console trace. 5) False positive rate kept under 3% on a 30-day historical test set.
tasks: Design autosampler strategy & sample budget (sequence-length stratification)
Prototype Bayesian sequential detector (Python) and benchmark on historical traces
Add a lightweight runner mode to bench-runner that accepts sample manifest and produces standard tokens/sec + latency telemetry
Integrate detector into GitHub Actions workflow with caching of compiled kernels to reduce cold-start variance
Persist sample-level results to metrics-store and add a compact PR-check visualization
Create rollout plan: opt-in orgs -> canary repos -> org-wide enforcement
Write docs for failure triage and adding new trace classes to the corpus

implementation_notes: Key design decisions: 1) Use a Bayesian sequential test (Beta/Bayesian bootstrap over tokens/sec) to allow early stopping with controlled Type I error. 2) Use stratified sampling across three sequence-length buckets (short/medium/long) and two prompt families (completion/dialogue). 3) Run each PR check in a deterministic container build to reduce variance from kernel compilation; use warm cache when available. 4) Threshold configuration exposed per-repo and centrally managed via perf-ci-config. 5) Store sample-level telemetry in metrics-store with tags: pr_id, commit_sha, seq_bucket, prompt_family, runner_variant. 6) Provide a manual "re-run with full baseline" button for on-demand deeper debugging.
notes_for_release: Canary rollout to infra-team repos for 2 weeks. If false positive rate < 3% and detection sensitivity meets acceptance, expand to customer-facing repos. Coordinate with runtime-1.20 release notes and include a short how-to in console docs.
